newsitem.title: CANADA: Slight downgrade seen on Manitoba's fusarium wheat.
newsitem.headline: Slight downgrade seen on Manitoba's fusarium wheat.

text.p: Some minor downgrades in Manitoba's spring wheat crop were expected from an outbreak of fusarium head blight, a grain quality specialist with Manitoba's largest grain handling firm said on Monday.

"It's not a severe outbreak where you're getting large percentages," Manitoba Pool Elevators quality control manager Derry Sager told Reuters. "You'll get some fields that may be hit a little harder than others but it's generally a No1 and No2 (Canada Western) Red (Spring Wheat) crop in southern Manitoba where the problem would be."
Fusarium is caused by prolonged rain during heading stage.
The fungus can produce vomitoxin which, in low levels, is tolerable, but in higher concentrations can cause nausea.

"We're not seeing anything big like 15 to 20 percent infected crops this year. We're seeing something very minute, either under 0.2 or not much over two percent if there is any heavier infestations," Sager said.
This summer's infection appeared to be most acute in the Red River Valley, Sager said.

The Canadian Grain Commission earlier this month estimated about two percent of early-harvested samples showed minor downgrading due to fusarium head blight. The CGC plans to update its estimate later this week.
MPE operates the largest number of primary elevators in Manitoba at more than 110.
